name: in-line-alert
description: In-line alerts display a non-modal message associated with objects in a view. These are often used in form validation, providing a place to aggregate feedback related to multiple fields.

documentBlocks.content: In-line alerts display a non-modal message associated with objects in a view. These are often used in form validation, providing a place to aggregate feedback related to multiple fields.

Text overflow.

When the title of an in-line alert is too long for the available horizontal space, it wraps to form another line. The optional icon in the top-right corner stays aligned to the top.

RTL.

For RTL (right-to-left) languages, the layout of the in-line alert is mirrored. The icon and dismiss button are both left-aligned.

style.description: The visual style of the alert.

href.description: Optional URL within in-line alert content like a 'Learn more' link.

heading.description: Optional heading text displayed at the top of the alert.

actionLabel.description: If undefined, this button does not appear.

anatomy.name: container
anatomy.description: Bordered or filled surface holding the alert content.

anatomy.name: title
anatomy.description: Alert heading. Hidden when no heading.

anatomy.name: button
anatomy.description: Optional action button, shown with actionLabel.

anatomyReview.notes: Owner decisions (A137, 2026-11-20): explicit root part container; text parts are title and description (Figma Heading and Content); link and button are separate parts. The style option picks the container fill (Figma 'Border fill' is the outline value, 'Subtle fill' subtle, 'Bold fill' bold). The 27 combined 'X and Icon' colour records are split into a container record and an icon record sharing one $ref; the icon is absent for the neutral variant (presentWhen is not built yet, so the part carries no condition). Edge padding uses axis endpoints (start-edge, end-edge, top-edge, bottom-edge) to content. Figma S2 Web In-line alert.
